title: Dynamic Batch Configurator: workload-aware continuous batching and safe rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a Dynamic Batch Configurator service that profiles live request shapes and suggests continuous batching parameters and cache policies. The configurator will produce safe, incremental config changes and automated rollback triggers to reduce per-token cost without increasing tail latency or degrading quality. This ticket covers the engine for profiling, heuristic scoring, and a guarded apply/rollback mechanism (not the UI).
background: We have several one-off batching heuristics in prod and a fingerprinting rollout (ENG-10345) but lack a continuously-running service that aggregates per-route profiles, scores candidate batching configs, and applies changes safely. Many customers show cost variability across times of day and sequence-length mixes; automated adjustments with safe rollback should capture savings while preserving SLOs.
design_decisions: Maintain per-route workload histograms (seq_len, request_rate, model_variant) with 1h and 24h windows
Score candidate configs using a weighted cost-latency utility: delta_cost_per_token + lambda * delta_p99_latency
Limit any single apply to <= 15% config change (e.g., batch size, max_concurrency, cache TTL) to avoid sudden behavior shifts
Apply changes via canary on 5% traffic with 30m observation window before broader rollout
Rollback triggers: p99 increase > 20ms OR error rate increase > 0.5% OR quality regressions from scripted prompts
Persist all config proposals and telemetry to S3/warehouse for audit and offline analysis
acceptance_criteria: Configurator collects stable per-route histograms for at least 90% of active routes within 24h
Simulator can predict cost and p99 change for a candidate config within 10% of observed after apply in 80% of trials
Safe apply flow: canary -> monitor -> promote/rollback automated end-to-end in staging using synthetic traffic
Automated rollback fires within the specified observation window when thresholds are exceeded
A proposal log exists with commit hashes, proposer, and telemetry snapshots for every automated change
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument runtime to emit compact per-route metrics (seq_len buckets, tokens, requests, p50/p95/p99 latency)
2) Build a lightweight profile aggregator service that stores 1h/24h histograms and exposes an API to query hot routes
3) Implement candidate generator: enumerate safe changes to batch_size, max_prefetch, kv_cache_ttl, and micro-batching window
4) Create a simulator module that replays recent traces against candidate configs to estimate cost and latency deltas
5) Implement a guarded apply controller: create canary config, route fraction, observe thresholds, promote or rollback
6) Add audit trail and metrics in Console for visibility (link to dashboard in links)
7) End-to-end staging test and incremental rollout to production
rollout_plan: Staging: run configurator against staging fleet for 2 weeks with synthetic traffic and manual verification
Phase 1: opt-in on low-risk routes (non-enterprise, short sequences) with canary 5% and 30m window
Phase 2: expand to 25% traffic after stable metrics for 48h
Phase 3: enable for all opt-in routes with automatic promotion disabled for enterprise-tier customers (manual approval)
testing_plan: Unit tests for histogram aggregation and candidate generation
Simulator integration tests using traces from production (anonymized)
End-to-end staging run verifying rollback triggers using injected faults
Load test to ensure aggregator and controller scale to 10k routes
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed — validated compact histogram schema and estimated storage cost (approx 20GB/day).
2026-02-20: Prototype simulator built; initial predictions correlated with small-scale experiments (median error ~12%).
2026-03-01: Guarded apply controller skeleton merged; canary routing hooks added to runtime (feature flag gated).
2026-03-10: Staging run started for 50 routes; observed cost reduction ~6% on those routes without p99 regression.

2026-03-14: Discovered an edge-case where micro-batching increased tail latency under bursty arrival; added a burst-detection rule to avoid applying micro-batch increases for routes with high arrival variance.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Config oscillation causing instability — Mitigation: enforce min cool-down (2h) between applies per-route
Risk: Silent quality regressions — Mitigation: include a small set of regression prompts per-customer and check semantic similarity pre/post
Risk: Storage and processing cost of fine-grained histograms — Mitigation: compact bucketing and retention pruning (keep 1h buckets for 7 days, 24h for 90 days)
